title_en: Yu Caixin v. Fujian Huachen Real Estate Co., Ltd. and Wei Chuanrui — dispute over a commercial housing sale (preliminary) contract
ruling_gist_en: According to the principle of privity of contract, if a party to the contract in question claims to exercise the right to suspend performance during the performance of the contract on the ground that a third party has breached a contract, the people's court shall not support such claim.

full_text_en:
Yu Caixin v. Fujian Huachen Real Estate Co., Ltd. and Wei Chuanrui — Dispute over a Contract for the Sale of Commercial Housing (Preliminary Contract)

Ruling Summary

In accordance with the principle of privity of contract, if a party to a contract involved in a case claims to exercise the right to suspend performance on the ground that a third party has breached the contract, the people's court shall not support such claim.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2010) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 13

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Yu Caixin, male, born on February 4, 1968, Han nationality, residing at Room 1408, No. 219, Jiangbin Middle Road, Yanping District, Nanping City, Fujian Province.

Agent ad litem: Tian Min, lawyer of Beijing Huizhong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Luo Huiyong, lawyer of Fujian Haochen Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Fujian Huachen Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Floors 10-12, Hualian Commercial Building, No. 47, Taijiang Road, Taijiang District, Fuzhou City, Fujian Province.

Legal Representative: Cai Hong, General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Han Mei, lawyer of Beijing Deheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Han Wei, female, Han nationality, born on November 11, 1982, residing at No. 87, Mingshui Baiyun Road, Zhangqiu City, Shandong Province.

Defendant at First Instance: Wei Chuanrui, male, born on October 28, 1959, resident of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, ID Card No. P018353(2), currently residing at Floor 12, Hualian Commercial Building, No. 47, Taijiang Road, Taijiang District, Fuzhou City, Fujian Province.

Agent ad litem: Han Mei, lawyer of Beijing Deheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Jianning, lawyer of Beijing Deheng Law Firm.

In the case of dispute over a contract for the sale of commercial housing (preliminary contract) between appellant Yu Caixin and appellant Fujian Huachen Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huachen Company) and defendant at first instance Wei Chuanrui, the Fujian High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2009) Min Min Chu Zi No. 8 on October 27, 2009. Dissatisfied with the judgment, both Yu Caixin and Huachen Company appealed to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing on April 19, 2010. Tian Min, agent ad litem of Yu Caixin; Han Mei and Han Wei, agents ad litem of Huachen Company; and Han Mei, agent ad litem of Wei Chuanrui, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The Fujian High People's Court found at first instance: On December 10, 2007, Party A Huachen Company, Party B Yu Caixin, and Party C Wei Chuanrui signed the "Shop Subscription Agreement" stipulating that Yu Caixin subscribed from Huachen Company the first, second, and third floor shops of Plot No. 1 of the "Junlin Shengshi Chating" project, with an area of approximately 2,378 square meters, at a unit price of RMB 72,798 per square meter, and a total price of RMB 172,750,198. Yu Caixin shall pay a deposit of RMB 63.6 million to Huachen Company within 10 days after signing this Subscription Agreement; Huachen Company shall obtain the "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit" within 30 days after receiving the deposit from Yu Caixin, and sign a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" with Yu Caixin, and simultaneously ensure that it is registered with the real estate transaction management department within 10 days after signing the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract". If Huachen Company fails to obtain the "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit" within the agreed time limit, Yu Caixin shall abandon the subscription, and Huachen Company must return all the deposit paid by Yu Caixin within two months from the 31st day after receiving the deposit; if the return is overdue, interest shall be calculated at a monthly rate of 10% (if less than one month, calculated on an actual day basis). If Huachen Company fails to return the full deposit within two months from the 31st day after receiving the deposit, it shall be deemed as overdue return; if the full deposit and its interest are not returned within three months after the overdue period, Yu Caixin may realize his claim by means of "using the house to offset the debt," i.e., converting the deposit and interest still owed by Huachen Company into purchasing the property of the above project of Huachen Company (the specific shop numbers to be selected by Yu Caixin), and the price of the shops shall be 30% of the selling price agreed in Article 1. If after such "house-for-debt" offset, Huachen Company still owes a balance to Yu Caixin, then Huachen Company shall provide shops from other plots to offset the remaining debt (still at 30% of the selling price), and the parties shall sign a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract". If Yu Caixin does not agree to realize the claim by means of "using the house to offset the debt," then Huachen Company shall repay in cash. The deposit of RMB 63.6 million paid by Yu Caixin shall be partly in cash and partly by remittance, etc. Wei Chuanrui shall bear joint and several liability for Huachen Company's debts, with a limitation period of two years.

After the signing of the above Shop Subscription Agreement, Yu Caixin or entities designated by him paid a total of RMB 49 million to Huachen Company through bank accounts in eight installments, specifically: one payment of RMB 20 million on December 10, 2007; two payments of RMB 9 million and RMB 4 million on December 11, 2007; two payments of RMB 8 million and RMB 2 million on December 20, 2007; two payments of RMB 4 million and RMB 1 million on December 21, 2007; and one payment of RMB 1 million on January 7, 2008. In the "Additional Information and Purpose" or "Purpose" columns of the above eight bank "Payment Vouchers," the voucher for RMB 8 million on December 20, 2007 indicated "working capital," the voucher for RMB 4 million on December 21, 2007 had a blank column, and the corresponding columns of the remaining six vouchers all indicated "loan." Correspondingly, Huachen Company issued six "Receipts" totaling RMB 49 million, specifically: one receipt for RMB 20 million on December 10, 2007; one receipt for RMB 13 million on December 11, 2007; three receipts for RMB 10 million, RMB 4 million, and RMB 1 million respectively on December 21, 2007, totaling RMB 15 million; and one receipt for RMB 1 million on January 7, 2008. In addition, Huachen Company also issued three "Receipts" to Yu Caixin on December 10, 2007, December 11, 2007, and December 21, 2007 for RMB 4 million, RMB 2.6 million, and RMB 3 million, totaling RMB 9.6 million. Thus, Huachen Company issued a total of nine "Receipts" to Yu Caixin totaling RMB 58.6 million. In the "Item Content" column of these nine "Receipts," it was written: "Deposit for subscription of first to third floor shops of Plot No. 1, Junlin Shengshi Chating (see agreement dated December 10, 2007 for details)," etc. In the stubs of the three "Receipts" totalling RMB 9.6 million (RMB 4 million, RMB 2.6 million, and RMB 3 million), in addition to the content "Deposit for subscription of first to third floor shops of Plot No. 1, Junlin Shengshi Chating (see agreement dated December 10, 2007 for details)," they also respectively noted "return rate part 2% extra," "return rate part 20% extra," and "100 + 1000 + 400 = 15 million return rate 20%."

The first instance court further found that Huachen Company obtained the "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit" for the disputed shops on June 26, 2008.

Yu Caixin filed a complaint with the first instance court, alleging that on December 10, 2007, as Party B, he signed a "Shop Subscription Agreement" with Party A Huachen Company and Party C Wei Chuanrui, stipulating the purchase of the first, second, and third floor shops of Plot No. 1 of the real estate project "Junlin Shengshi Chating" developed by Huachen Company, with an area of 2,378 square meters, at a unit price of RMB 72,798 per square meter, and a total price of RMB 172,750,198. Party B shall pay a deposit of RMB 63.6 million to Party A within 10 days after signing this Subscription Agreement; Party A shall obtain the "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit" within 30 days after receiving Party B's deposit and sign a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" with Party B, and shall register it with the real estate transaction management department within 10 days after signing the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract". If Party A fails to obtain the "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit" within the agreed time limit, Party B shall abandon the subscription, and Party A must return the full deposit to Party B within two months from the 31st day after receiving the deposit; if the return is overdue, Party A shall pay principal and interest at a monthly rate of 10% to Party B. If Party A fails to return the full deposit within two months from the 31st day after receiving the deposit, it shall be deemed as overdue return; if the full deposit and its interest are not returned within three months after the overdue period, Party B may realize his claim by means of "using the house to offset the debt," and the shop price shall be 30% of the selling price agreed in this Subscription Agreement. If Party B does not agree to realize the claim by means of "using the house to offset the debt," then Party A shall repay in cash. Party C shall bear joint and several liability for Party A's debts, with a limitation period of two years. The Subscription Agreement also contained provisions regarding Party B's payment methods, etc. After the contract was signed, Yu Caixin paid RMB 58.6 million to Huachen Company in installments as the purchase price, to which Huachen Company raised no objection. During the payment period, Yu Caixin learned that Huachen Company was unable to obtain the "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit" on schedule, so he temporarily suspended payment of the remaining deposit of RMB 5 million, which was in compliance with Article 68 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law). After repeated reminders, Huachen Company refused to sign a "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" with Yu Caixin on various pretexts, and subsequently resold the shops under the Shop Subscription Agreement to others, making it impossible for Huachen Company to perform. In summary, Huachen Company's conduct violated Article 60 of the Contract Law and Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Contracts for the Sale of Commercial Housing, and should bear liability for breach of contract. Wei Chuanrui's conduct violated the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China. His amended claims were: (1) rescind the "Shop Subscription Agreement" signed by the parties; (2) Huachen Company return the purchase deposit of RMB 58.6 million; (3) Huachen Company pay liquidated damages at 10% per month on the deposit paid by Yu Caixin, calculated from March 22, 2008 until the date of full repayment, tentatively calculated up to March 22, 2009 as RMB 70.32 million (RMB 58.6 million x 12 months x 10% = RMB 70.32 million); (4) Wei Chuanrui bear joint and several liability for Huachen Company's debts under items (2) and (3) above; (5) Huachen Company and Wei Chuanrui bear the litigation costs of this case.

Huachen Company responded at first instance, arguing that there was no shop subscription between Huachen Company and Yu Caixin; Huachen Company's sale of shops to others was unrelated to Yu Caixin. The actual relationship between the parties was a loan. The amount lent by Yu Caixin was only RMB 49 million transferred through bank accounts. Yu Caixin's claim of an additional cash payment of RMB 9.6 million was false; that RMB 9.6 million was the 20% return (interest) on the loan of RMB 49 million. Yu Caixin's claim of paying RMB 58.6 million to Huachen Company was untrue. The "Shop Subscription Agreement" was a contract that uses a lawful form to conceal the illegal purpose of usury, and therefore was void. Even if the Shop Subscription Agreement were valid, Yu Caixin failed to pay the deposit of RMB 63.6 million within 10 days as stipulated, constituting a prior breach. Huachen Company was entitled to refuse to perform obligations such as obtaining the "Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit," and Yu Caixin's claim for Huachen Company to bear liability for breach of contract was unfounded. Huachen Company requested the court to find that the relationship between the parties was a loan, with the principal being RMB 49 million.

Wei Chuanrui responded at first instance, arguing that this case was a loan dispute, and there was no shop subscription relationship between the parties. The December 10, 2007 "Shop Subscription Agreement" used a lawful form to conceal the illegal purpose of usury and should be declared void. The guarantee contract is an ancillary contract; if the principal contract is void, the guarantee contract is certainly void, and Wei Chuanrui is not liable for the repayment guarantee in this case. He requested the court to dismiss Yu Caixin's claim for Wei Chuanrui to bear guarantee liability.

On March 11, 2009, the first instance court, based on Yu Caixin's application for property preservation, issued a civil ruling (2009) Min Min Chu Zi No. 8, freezing the land use rights of Plots He 3, 5, 7, and 8 (land certificates: Rong Guo Yong No. 32334400071, 32334500073, 32334600075, 32434500076) of the "Junlin Shengshi Chating" project under Huachen Company's name. After two modifications, the order was changed to freeze the shops on the second and third floors of the eastern part of Plot Seven of the Junlin Shengshi Chating project under Huachen Company's name.

The first instance court held that the parties disputed the nature of the RMB 58.6 million recorded in the Receipts issued by Huachen Company and the actual amount received by Huachen Company. Yu Caixin argued that the RMB 58.6 million was the deposit paid in performance of the Shop Subscription Agreement signed by the parties, of which RMB 49 million was paid through bank accounts, and the remaining RMB 9.6 million was paid in cash in three installments, i.e., on December 10, 2007, December 11, 2007, and December 21, 2007, he paid Huachen Company RMB 4 million, RMB 2.6 million, and RMB 3 million respectively. This RMB 9.6 million was raised from relatives and Nanping Rongxin Materials Recycling Co., Ltd., as evidenced by relevant bank transfers, cash source vouchers for RMB 9.6 million, and the Receipts issued by Huachen Company. Huachen Company and Wei Chuanrui argued that: (1) Huachen Company actually only received the RMB 49 million paid by Yu Caixin through bank accounts; Yu Caixin's claim of an additional cash payment of RMB 9.6 million in three installments was false. In fact, Huachen Company issued not only these three Receipts for RMB 9.6 million but also one for RMB 200,000, which Yu Caixin did not produce; the four Receipts totaling RMB 9.8 million represented the 20% return (interest) on a three-month loan of RMB 49 million. (2) The loan relationship between Huachen Company and Yu Caixin could also be corroborated by the following facts: Article 3 of the Shop Subscription Agreement stipulated that if Huachen Company failed to return the full deposit within two months from the 31st day after receiving the deposit, it should pay 10% interest; Article 4 stipulated that if the deposit and interest were not fully returned within three months after the overdue period, the debt should be offset by a house at 30% of the price; Yu Caixin had recorded the purpose of the payment as "loan" on some bank transfer vouchers; Huachen Company noted "return rate" or "loan return rate" on the stubs and ledgers of the RMB 9.6 million Receipts; and Yu Caixin's original complaint (before amending claims) requested Huachen Company to pay default interest at four times the benchmark loan interest rate of the same period of the bank. All these facts could prove that the legal relationship disputed by the parties was a loan, with the principal being RMB 49 million, not RMB 58.6 million. The first instance court held that Huachen Company issued nine Receipts to Yu Caixin, confirming the receipt of RMB 58.6 million based on the Shop Subscription Agreement; the nature of the payment should be determined as the deposit under the Shop Subscription Agreement. Pursuant to Article 5 of the Shop Subscription Agreement, Yu Caixin's payment of the deposit was partly in cash and partly by bank transfer. Therefore, Yu Caixin's claim that RMB 49 million of the above RMB 58.6 million was by bank transfer and RMB 9.6 million was paid in cash was consistent with common sense and should be accepted. The facts that some of Yu Caixin's bank transfer vouchers recorded the purpose of the payment as "loan," that Huachen Company noted "return rate" or "loan return rate" on the stubs and ledgers of the RMB 9.6 million Receipts, and that Yu Caixin calculated liquidated damages based on interest in his complaint, were insufficient to prove that the actual payment by Yu Caixin was RMB 49 million or that the relevant payments were in the nature of a loan. Accordingly, it should be determined that Yu Caixin paid a deposit of RMB 58.6 million under the Shop Subscription Agreement.

Pursuant to Article 16 of the Measures for the Administration of Commercial Housing Sales, when selling commercial housing, a real estate development enterprise and the buyer shall conclude a written commercial housing sales contract specifying the main terms of the transaction. In this case, the Shop Subscription Agreement entered into by the parties stipulated core terms such as the location, area, unit price, and total price of the commercial housing to be sold, which is consistent with the basic characteristics of a commercial housing sales contract. However, because the Shop Subscription Agreement also expressly provided that after Huachen Company obtained the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit, a separate commercial housing sales contract should be signed, and the content was lacking in many aspects compared with the provisions of Article 16 of the Measures for the Administration of Commercial Housing Sales, it should be determined that the Shop Subscription Agreement was a prior agreement reached by the parties for the future signing of a shop sales contract, and this case is a dispute over a contract for the sale of commercial housing (preliminary contract). Huachen Company's claim that this case was a loan dispute was insufficiently evidenced and was not accepted.

The Shop Subscription Agreement involved in the case was the true expression of the parties' intentions, and its content did not violate the prohibitive provisions of national laws or administrative regulations; it should be deemed valid. According to the content of Articles 2 and 3 of the Subscription Agreement, Yu Caixin should pay a deposit of RMB 63.6 million to Huachen Company within 10 days after signing the Subscription Agreement; Huachen Company should obtain the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit within 30 days after receiving the deposit from Yu Caixin; otherwise, it must return the full deposit to Yu Caixin within two months from the 31st day after receiving the deposit; if the return is overdue, principal and interest shall be paid at a monthly rate of 10%. Accordingly, the performance period for Huachen Company to obtain the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit was within 30 days after Yu Caixin paid the full RMB 63.6 million. Since Yu Caixin only paid a deposit of RMB 58.6 million, even if during the payment of the deposit there was a situation where Yu Caixin exercised the right to suspend performance due to Huachen Company's inability to obtain the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit on schedule, leading to the non-payment of the full deposit, Huachen Company would not constitute a breach. Because after Yu Caixin learned that Huachen Company had obtained the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit on June 26, 2008, there was no evidence that he subsequently requested Huachen Company to continue paying the remaining deposit, and in fact he did not pay it. Therefore, it should be determined that Yu Caixin has not paid the full deposit of RMB 63.6 million as agreed, and Huachen Company obtained the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit within the performance period stipulated in the Shop Subscription Agreement. Yu Caixin's claim that Huachen Company should bear liquidated damages at a monthly rate of 10% on the deposit of RMB 58.6 million paid by Yu Caixin, on the grounds that Huachen Company delayed in obtaining the Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit and failed to return the full deposit within two months from the 31st day after receiving the deposit, lacked factual basis. The first instance court did not support this claim.

Yu Caixin, claiming that the disputed shops had been sold by Huachen Company to others, requested the rescission of the Shop Subscription Agreement. Huachen Company and Wei Chuanrui did not dispute the fact that the shops had been sold to others. Since continued performance of the Shop Subscription Agreement was impossible, it should be rescinded according to law. The deposit of RMB 58.6 million and its statutory interest collected by Huachen Company under the Shop Subscription Agreement should be returned. Yu Caixin's request to rescind the Shop Subscription Agreement and for Huachen Company to return the collected deposit of RMB 58.6 million should be supported. Huachen Company shall return to Yu Caixin the shop deposit of RMB 58.6 million and pay interest calculated from the date of receipt of the relevant sums. Wei Chuanrui, as one of the parties signing the Shop Subscription Agreement, was willing to provide a two-year joint and several guarantee liability for Huachen Company's performance of the relevant debts under the subscription agreement. According to Article 18 of the Guarantee Law of the PRC concerning joint and several guarantee, Wei Chuanrui shall bear joint and several liability for Huachen Company's obligation to return RMB 58.6 million and its interest to Yu Caixin. The court of first instance, in accordance with Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, Article 94 of the Contract Law, and Article 18 of the Guarantee Law of the PRC, adjudged as follows: 1. Rescind the Shop Subscription Agreement entered into by the three parties; 2. Huachen Company shall pay to Yu Caixin RMB 58.6 million and interest thereon (calculated from December 10, 2007 for RMB 24 million, from December 11, 2007 for RMB 15.6 million, from December 21, 2007 for RMB 18 million, and from January 7, 2008 for RMB 1 million, up to the date of repayment as determined in this judgment, at the corresponding loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period) within ten days from the effective date of this judgment; 3. Wei Chuanrui shall bear joint and several repayment liability for Huachen Company's debt under item 2 above; 4. Dismiss Yu Caixin's other claims. Court acceptance fee of RMB 686,400, to be borne by Yu Caixin in the amount of RMB 356,400, and by Huachen Company and Wei Chuanrui in the amount of RMB 330,000; litigation preservation fee of RMB 5,000, to be borne by Yu Caixin in the amount of RMB 3,000, and by Huachen Company and Wei Chuanrui in the amount of RMB 2,000.

Yu Caixin and Huachen Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, respectively appealed to this Court.

Yu Caixin appealed, arguing that the judgment of first instance had unclear fact-finding, improper application of law, and clearly imbalanced outcome. He therefore requested: (1) Set aside items 2 and 4 of the civil judgment (2009) Min Chu Zi No. 8; (2) Order Huachen Company to return to Yu Caixin the house purchase deposit of RMB 58.6 million, and pay liquidated damages at the rate of 10% per month of the deposit already paid by Yu Caixin, calculated from March 22, 2008 until the date of full payment (provisionally calculated as RMB 70.32 million as of March 22, 2009). The main facts and reasons were:

(I) The fact-finding in the judgment of first instance was unclear. 1. The time for Huachen Company to obtain the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing as stipulated in the contract as found by the judgment of first instance did not conform to objective facts. According to the Shop Subscription Agreement, Yu Caixin was to pay Huachen Company a deposit of RMB 63.6 million within 10 days; Huachen Company was to obtain the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing within 30 days after receiving Yu Caixin's deposit and enter into a formal Commercial Housing Sale Contract with Yu Caixin, and at the same time ensure registration for the record with the real estate transaction management department within 10 days after signing the Commercial Housing Sale Contract. The Shop Subscription Agreement was signed on December 10, 2007, so the deadline for Huachen Company to obtain the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing should have been before January 21, 2008. This fact was not disputed by either party during the trial of first instance, and was not the performance period found by the judgment of first instance, namely "within 30 days after Yu Caixin pays off RMB 63.6 million." 2. The finding in the judgment of first instance that "Yu Caixin knew that Huachen Company obtained the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing on June 26, 2008" did not conform to objective facts. After Yu Caixin paid the house purchase deposit of RMB 58.6 million and performed his main obligation, because Huachen Company failed to obtain the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing before January 21, 2008 as required by the contract, and because Fuzhou Huachen Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Fuzhou Huachen Company), which was actually controlled by Wei Chuanrui, had engaged in fraudulent conduct when signing the contract with Yu Caixin for the purchase of "Shop No. 23 on the 2nd Floor of the Connected Building 5#7# of B Group, Junlin Tianhua," Yu Caixin did not continue to pay the remaining RMB 5 million. Moreover, after Huachen Company failed to obtain the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing as stipulated in the contract, it never informed Yu Caixin when it could obtain the permit, nor did it inform Yu Caixin after it obtained the permit. It also did not provide evidence during the trial of first instance to prove this fact. It was only after Huachen Company had sold the shops stipulated in the Shop Subscription Agreement to others, before filing the lawsuit, that Yu Caixin, under the guidance of his lawyer, discovered on January 7, 2009 from the Fuzhou Real Estate Information Network that Huachen Company had obtained a pre-sale permit for the commercial complex on Lot A Block 1, with an approval date of June 26, 2008. This fact could be proven by Evidence 11 submitted by Yu Caixin in the first instance. Therefore, the finding in the judgment of first instance that "Yu Caixin knew that Huachen Company obtained the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing on June 26, 2008" did not conform to objective facts, and the conclusion that Yu Caixin did not pay off the RMB 63.6 million as contracted and that Huachen Company did not breach the contract was contrary to objective facts.

(II) The application of law in the judgment of first instance was improper. 1. Yu Caixin had the right to exercise the right of suspension of performance (right of insecurity defense). Because Huachen Company did not obtain the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing within the time stipulated in the contract, Yu Caixin suspended payment of the remaining RMB 5 million, which was in accordance with Article 68 of the Contract Law. Yu Caixin had evidence that Huachen Company had lost commercial credit and had other circumstances that might lead to inability to perform its debts. Yu Caixin had signed a contract on August 3, 2007 with Fuzhou Huachen Company, which was actually controlled by Wei Chuanrui, agreeing to purchase the "Shop No. 23 on the 2nd Floor of the Connected Building 5#7# of B Group, Junlin Tianhua" owned by it. After Yu Caixin paid the full amount in cash as stipulated in the contract, Fuzhou Huachen Company violated Article 24 of the contract by failing to apply for registration for the record with the Fuzhou Real Estate Transaction Registration Center within 30 days after the contract took effect. Later, Yu Caixin learned from the Fuzhou Real Estate Information Network and inquiries with the Fuzhou Real Estate Transaction Registration Center that the commercial housing under the contract was used for mortgage loans. Accordingly, Yu Caixin's failure to pay the remaining purchase price of RMB 5 million to Huachen Company was in compliance with relevant legal provisions. 2. The reason for the rescission of the Shop Subscription Agreement in this case was the fundamental breach by Huachen Company. Yu Caixin had paid 92.14% of the purchase price and performed the main obligations under the contract. Huachen Company had fundamentally breached the contract, and the judgment of first instance was clearly unfair.

Huachen Company appealed, arguing that the judgment of first instance had unclear fact-finding and errors in the application of law. It therefore requested this Court: (1) Set aside item 2 of the judgment of first instance in this case, and amend the judgment to order that Huachen Company only needs to return to Yu Caixin the house purchase deposit of RMB 49 million; (2) Order Yu Caixin to bear all litigation costs in this case. The main facts and reasons were:

(I) Yu Caixin actually only paid RMB 49 million in house purchase deposit to Huachen Company. According to the Shop Subscription Agreement, Yu Caixin was to pay a house purchase deposit of RMB 63.6 million to Huachen Company within 10 days after the signing of the subscription agreement, i.e., before December 21, 2007. In the first instance, Yu Caixin provided Receipts to prove payment of RMB 58.6 million in house purchase deposit to Huachen Company. However, according to the bank transfer slips provided by both parties, Yu Caixin paid a total of RMB 49 million in house purchase deposit to Huachen Company through bank transfers. In the first instance, Yu Caixin claimed to have paid an additional RMB 9.6 million in cash. But when Huachen Company repeatedly requested Yu Caixin during the trial to explain the time, place, and recipient of the delivery of this RMB 9.6 million in cash, Yu Caixin and his agents could not give a direct answer. A huge sum of nearly ten million yuan was not transferred through bank channels, and the circumstances of delivery could not be explained; this was clearly not consistent with common sense. In substance, it was interest generated on the RMB 49 million. It was thus evident that the cash payment of RMB 9.6 million claimed by Yu Caixin did not exist at all. Since he only paid RMB 49 million in house purchase deposit to Huachen Company, the judgment of first instance, which found that Yu Caixin paid RMB 58.6 million in house purchase deposit to Huachen Company and ordered Huachen Company to return RMB 58.6 million in house purchase deposit, was erroneous and should be corrected.

(II) Due to Yu Caixin's fault, the Shop Subscription Agreement could not be performed and was rescinded. Huachen Company only needed to refund the RMB 49 million and did not need to pay interest.

The facts found by this Court on second-instance review were consistent with those found by the court of first instance.

During the second-instance review, this Court organized mediation between the parties to this case, but mediation failed due to significant disagreements over the facts and liability for liquidated damages.

Opinion of the Court

The court of first instance classified the nature of this case as a dispute over a commercial housing sale (pre-sale) contract, and, based on Yu Caixin's claim, ruled to rescind the contract. The three parties did not appeal this point, and this Court confirms it. Huachen Company and Wei Chuanrui do not dispute that Huachen Company received a deposit of RMB 49 million transferred by Yu Caixin, and this Court confirms that. The issues in dispute between the parties in this second-instance review are: (1) Whether Yu Caixin paid a cash deposit of RMB 9.6 million for the house purchase to Huachen Company; (2) Whether Yu Caixin's short payment of RMB 5 million in deposit constituted an exercise of the right of insecurity defense; (3) Whether Huachen Company should bear liability for breach of contract. These issues are discussed separately below.

(1) Regarding whether Yu Caixin paid a cash deposit of RMB 9.6 million for the house purchase to Huachen Company.

Opinion of the Court: Based on the facts found, it should be determined that Yu Caixin did pay a cash deposit of RMB 9.6 million for the house purchase to Huachen Company. The reasons are: 1. The Shop Subscription Agreement stipulated that part of the deposit of RMB 63.6 million to be paid by Yu Caixin was in cash and part by remittance. Therefore, Yu Caixin's payment of RMB 9.6 million in cash to Huachen Company as a house purchase deposit was in accordance with the contract. 2. After receiving the RMB 9.6 million in cash delivered by Yu Caixin, Huachen Company issued a Receipt to Yu Caixin. Huachen Company did not dispute the authenticity of the receipt itself. The receipt stated that the payment was for the purchase of the house under the contract in question. The Receipt submitted by Yu Caixin to the courts of first and second instance did not record a "rate of return," while the counterfoil of the Receipt issued by Huachen Company recorded a "rate of return," indicating that this was added later by Huachen Company on the counterfoil. The Receipt provided by Yu Caixin should be used as the basis for finding the facts. 3. The added "rate of return" on the Receipts was contradictory, with some being 2% and others 20%. Calculated according to either of the above percentages, the conclusion that RMB 9.6 million in interest was generated from a loan of RMB 49 million could not be reached. 4. Although Huachen Company denied that Yu Caixin paid it RMB 9.6 million in cash, it had insufficient evidence to overturn the Receipt it issued to Yu Caixin. Although the place of payment described by Yu Caixin was unusual, this possibility cannot be excluded. In summary, Huachen Company's claim that Yu Caixin did not pay it RMB 9.6 million in cash was insufficiently supported by evidence, and this Court does not support it.

(2) Regarding whether Yu Caixin's short payment of RMB 5 million in deposit constituted an exercise of the right of insecurity defense.

Opinion of the Court: The basis for Yu Caixin's claim of the right of insecurity defense was that Huachen Company had lost commercial credit, based on the fact that after he signed another house purchase contract with Fuzhou Huachen Company, Fuzhou Huachen Company mortgaged the house under the contract. However, Fuzhou Huachen Company and Huachen Company are two different legal persons. Exercising the right of insecurity defense in the performance of the contract in this case based on a breach by a person not a party to the contract does not comply with the principle of privity of contract. According to Article 68 of the Contract Law, Yu Caixin's claim that he exercised the right of insecurity defense was insufficiently based. Article 69 of the Contract Law sets out the requirements for exercising the right of insecurity defense. Even if Yu Caixin had the right to exercise the right of insecurity defense, he should have promptly notified the other party. However, there is no evidence that Yu Caixin fulfilled the obligation to notify. Therefore, Yu Caixin's claim that he exercised the right of insecurity defense lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

(3) Regarding whether Huachen Company should bear liability for breach of contract.

Opinion of the Court: Although Yu Caixin claimed that he had paid most of the deposit, performed the main obligation of paying the deposit, and had the right of insecurity defense, according to the Shop Subscription Agreement, Huachen Company was to obtain the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing and sign the house purchase contract with Yu Caixin within 30 days after receiving Yu Caixin's deposit. Accordingly, it should be determined that Yu Caixin had a prior performance obligation. He should have paid off the deposit of RMB 63.6 million before December 20, 2007. However, to date, Yu Caixin has only paid RMB 58.6 million in deposit. His reason for claiming the right of insecurity defense cannot be established. Therefore, it should be determined that Yu Caixin breached the contract, and thus he has no right to claim liquidated damages from Huachen Company. Since Yu Caixin breached the contract first, even if Huachen Company later failed to timely obtain the Pre-sale Permit for Commercial Housing and sign the house purchase contract with Yu Caixin, it should not pay liquidated damages to Yu Caixin. After the Shop Subscription Agreement in this case is rescinded, the rights and obligations of the parties terminate. Since the property transaction was not completed, the property held by one party should be returned to the other party. Huachen Company holds Yu Caixin's house purchase deposit of RMB 58.6 million and the interest generated thereon, which should be returned together. Therefore, this Court does not support Huachen Company's claim that it should only return RMB 49 million in deposit to Yu Caixin.

In summary, the judgment of first instance had clear fact-finding and correct application of law. After the rescission of the Shop Subscription Agreement, Huachen Company and Wei Chuanrui shall return the deposit and interest to Yu Caixin. Since Yu Caixin breached the contract first, this Court does not support his request that Huachen Company pay him liquidated damages. Huachen Company's request that it should only return RMB 49 million in deposit to Yu Caixin lacks legal basis, and this Court does not support it. In accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

Dismiss the appeals and affirm the original judgment.

Court acceptance fee for the second instance of RMB 686,400, to be borne by Yu Caixin in the amount of RMB 565,000, and by Fujian Huachen Real Estate Co., Ltd. and Wei Chuanrui in the amount of RMB 121,400.

This judgment is final.
